title: EIP-7702 Authorization-Tuple Decoder
description: Recomputes the EIP-7702 authorization-tuple hash (keccak256(0x05 || rlp([chain_id, address, nonce])), the 'Set EOA account code' standard live on Ethereum mainnet since the Pectra upgrade, 2025-05-07), recovers the ECDSA signer from a caller-supplied signature, and reports the address the recovered signer is authorizing as its delegate. The tuple's own `address` field IS the delegate: the code the EOA is pointing itself at. This node stops at that address -- it never inspects, fetches, or judges the delegate contract's bytecode, and makes no safe/unsafe verdict about it. chain_id = 0 is EIP-7702-defined as a valid, deliberate cross-chain authorization (replayable on any chain) and is reported as such, never treated as malformed input. RLP encoding is hand-authored public-spec arithmetic (Ethereum Yellow Paper Appendix B); keccak256 and secp256k1 recovery come from the already-vendored, pinned noble-curves bundle, no new vendoring. Malformed or incomplete input produces a clean INDETERMINATE/RECOVERY_FAILED finding, never a thrown exception. Zero network calls: does not confirm the authorization was ever submitted on-chain, does not confirm the EOA's account nonce matches the declared nonce at any block, and makes no settlement claim.

chainId.description: Authorization-tuple chain_id. Mandatory. 0 is spec-valid and means a cross-chain authorization, replayable on any chain -- never treated as an error.

address.description: 20-byte hex address. Mandatory. The delegate the EOA is authorizing itself to point at -- reported as a plain fact, never analyzed.

signature.description: Full signature hex: 64 bytes (r||s, recovery id supplied separately via v/yParity) or 65 bytes (r||s||v, recovery marker embedded). Alternative to r/s.

r.description: 32-byte hex signature r value. Used with s when signature is not supplied.

s.description: 32-byte hex signature s value. Used with r when signature is not supplied.

v.description: Recovery marker: raw bit (0/1) or legacy Ethereum (27/28). EIP-7702 authorization tuples natively carry yParity; v is accepted for callers who paste a v-style value by habit.

yParity.description: Recovery marker as a raw bit (0/1), the authorization tuple's native field name. Takes precedence over v/embedded signature byte if supplied.

mcp_tool_definition.name: decode_eip7702_authorization_tuple
mcp_tool_definition.description: Recomputes the EIP-7702 authorization-tuple hash from declared (chain_id, address, nonce), recovers the ECDSA signer, and reports the address-only fact of the delegate the EOA is authorizing. Never judges the delegate's code. chain_id=0 (cross-chain) is disclosed, not treated as an error. No hand-rolled crypto; recovery via the vendored, pinned noble-curves bundle. Malformed input produces a structured refusal, never a thrown error. No on-chain-submission or settlement claim.

output_example.scope_note: Recomputes the EIP-7702 authorization-tuple hash from declared (chain_id, address, nonce) fields, recovers the ECDSA signer from the caller-supplied signature, and reports the address the recovered signer is authorizing as its delegate. Proves that a private key produced a valid signature over the exact tuple supplied -- it does NOT judge the delegate contract's code, does not confirm the authorization was ever submitted or applied on-chain, and does not confirm the recovered signer's account nonce matches the declared nonce at any block. An authorization is not a settlement, and a recovered delegate address is not a safety verdict. Zero network calls; never a facilitator, proxy, or settlement relay.
